paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The diagram illustrates the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, in relation to the number of in-context examples, with the y-axis labeled "minFDE20" and the x-axis labeled "Number of Examples". The y-axis ranges from 0.85 to 1.05, with tick labels at intervals of 0.05, while the x-axis ranges from 0 to 15, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The ST-ES line, represented in blue with a solid line and circular markers, starts at approximately 1.07 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 1 and decreases sharply to around 0.84 when the number of examples is 2; it then gradually decreases to about 0.78 when the number of examples is 15, with minor fluctuations in between, including a slight dip to 0.77 at 7 examples and a rise to 0.81 at 14 examples. The Random line, represented in orange with a solid line and circular markers, begins at around 1.03 on the y-axis when the number of examples is 1 and decreases to approximately 0.97 when the number of examples is 15, with some minor fluctuations in between, including a peak of 0.98 at 10 examples and a trough of 0.96 at 12 examples.

model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, in relation to the number of in-context examples. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," has a linear scale with a value range of 0 to 15 and is marked in intervals of 1. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE20," has a linear scale with a value range of 0.85 to 1.05 and is marked in intervals of 0.05. The plot contains two lines: the ST-ES line is blue with circular markers and a solid line style, starting at approximately 1.05 and decreasing to around 0.85, then remaining relatively stable with minor fluctuations around 0.83; the Random line is orange with circular markers and a solid line style, starting at approximately 1.02 and decreasing to around 0.98, then remaining relatively stable with minor fluctuations.
